items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha always shared her snacks with Ben. One day, Ben ate the last cookie without asking. Aisha walked away and did not say anything.

Why do you think Aisha walked away without saying anything? Use details from the story.
items.answer: Aisha was probably hurt or upset because she always shared with Ben, but he took her cookie without asking. She may have walked away to avoid saying something unkind.

steps: Aisha always shared, which shows she was a good friend. Ben did not ask, which was not fair. Walking away without saying anything can mean you are hurt but trying to stay calm. The contrast between how kind Aisha was and what Ben did explains her reaction.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco loved to draw. One day, his teacher put his drawing on the board in front of the class. Marco's face turned red. He looked at his shoes.

Why do you think Marco looked at his shoes? Is there more than one possible reason?
items.answer: Marco may have felt embarrassed or shy about having his work shown to everyone, even if he was also proud. Looking at his shoes shows he did not want to make eye contact.

steps: When people feel embarrassed or shy, they often look down and avoid eye contact. Marco's face turning red also shows a strong feeling. He might have felt proud that his work was chosen, but also shy about all the attention. Both feelings are possible at the same time.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe told her friend Sam a secret. The next day, everyone at school knew the secret. Sam did not look at Zoe at lunch.

What can you figure out from this story? Explain your thinking.
items.answer: Sam probably told the secret, and he knew it was wrong. He avoided looking at Zoe at lunch because he felt guilty.

steps: Zoe told only Sam the secret. Then everyone knew it. That means Sam most likely told. Sam not looking at Zoe suggests he felt guilty or knew he had done something wrong. Guilty people often avoid the person they hurt.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Every morning, Leo's grandma made him oatmeal. Leo always said it was too lumpy. But the day grandma was sick in bed, Leo made himself cereal. He missed his oatmeal.

What does this tell you about how Leo really felt about his grandma's oatmeal?
items.answer: Even though Leo complained about the oatmeal, he actually liked it and missed it when it was gone. The oatmeal made him feel cared for by his grandma.

steps: Leo said the oatmeal was lumpy, which sounds like a complaint. But when grandma was sick, he missed it. That means he actually liked it. People sometimes don't realize they like something until it is gone. The oatmeal probably also reminded him of his grandma's care.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Ben worked very hard on a sandcastle at the beach. Just before he finished, a big wave came and washed it all away. Ben sat quietly for a moment. Then he started building again.

What does Ben's reaction tell you about him?
items.answer: Ben is resilient. He felt sad when the wave destroyed his castle, but he did not give up. He chose to start over instead of quitting.

steps: Sitting quietly shows Ben was upset or sad. But starting over shows he did not give up. A person who keeps trying after something goes wrong is resilient. Ben's reaction tells us he is the kind of person who does not quit easily.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya's new neighbor moved in next door. Maya made a card with flowers on it and left it on the neighbor's porch. She did not sign her name.

Why do you think Maya did not sign her name?
items.answer: Maya may have been shy or wanted to be kind without getting credit for it. She wanted the neighbor to feel welcome but did not need them to know who did it.

steps: Making a card shows Maya wanted to be kind and welcoming. Not signing it means she did not need the neighbor to know it was her. This could mean she is shy, or it could mean she was doing a purely kind act without wanting anything in return. Both are reasonable explanations.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha's class got a new student named Omar. No one talked to Omar at recess. He stood by the fence alone. Aisha saw him and walked over.

Why did Aisha walk over to Omar? What does this tell you about her?
items.answer: Aisha walked over because she noticed Omar was alone and felt bad for him. This tells us she is kind and caring.

steps: Omar was alone and no one talked to him. Aisha noticed and chose to go to him. People who notice when others feel left out and do something about it are kind and empathetic. Aisha's action shows she is a caring person.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam wanted to win the race more than anything. When the race started, Sam ran as fast as he could. He saw his friend Leo fall down. Sam stopped to help Leo up. They came in last together.

Why did Sam stop? What did his choice show about him?
items.answer: Sam stopped because helping his friend was more important to him than winning. His choice shows he is a loyal and caring friend.

steps: The story says Sam wanted to win more than anything. But when Leo fell, Sam stopped. That was a hard choice because it cost him the race. Choosing a friend over winning shows Sam valued Leo's well-being more than the trophy. His choice reveals that he is a loyal, caring friend.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Every Friday, Leo's dad brought home pizza. One Friday, his dad came home late with no pizza. Leo said, 'That's okay, Dad. I'll help make dinner.'

How is Leo's reaction different from what you might expect? What does it show about him?
items.answer: You might expect Leo to be disappointed because he loves pizza. Instead he offered to help. This shows Leo is understanding and thoughtful.

steps: Leo loved pizza Fridays, so missing it could make him upset. But instead of complaining, he offered to help. This is unexpected and kind. It shows Leo understood his dad had a hard day and put his dad's feelings before his own disappointment.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe drew a picture and showed it to her little brother. He said it was ugly. Zoe put the picture in a drawer and never drew again that week.

What effect did her brother's words have on Zoe? Why is this important?
items.answer: Her brother's words hurt Zoe and made her stop drawing for a week. This shows that unkind words can stop people from doing things they enjoy.

steps: Zoe stopped drawing after her brother called her picture ugly. She hid her drawing in a drawer, which shows she felt ashamed or hurt. The effect was that she gave up something she liked. This matters because unkind words can have a big impact on how people feel about themselves and their work.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Ben noticed that his friend Marco was quiet and looked sad at lunch. Marco said he was fine, but Ben saved half his cookie for him anyway.

What question could you ask about this story, and what is the answer?
items.answer: A good question: Why did Ben save a cookie for Marco if Marco said he was fine? Answer: Ben could tell Marco was not really fine, so he wanted to show he cared through a kind act.

steps: A strong question looks beyond what is directly stated. Marco said he was fine, but the story tells us he was quiet and sad. Ben did not believe the words, he believed what he saw. Saving the cookie was a way of showing Marco he was seen and cared for, even without saying so.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha had practiced her song for the school show for two weeks. When the day came, she stood behind the curtain. Her hands were shaking and her heart was pounding.

Why were Aisha's hands shaking even though she had practiced a lot?
items.answer: Aisha was nervous about performing in front of an audience. Practice prepares you, but it does not always stop nerves before a big moment.

steps: Shaking hands and a pounding heart are signs of nervousness. Aisha practiced, so she knew the song. But practicing alone is different from performing in front of people. The audience makes it a much bigger moment, which can cause nerves even when you are prepared.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam's family moved to a new town. At his new school, Sam sat at the back of the class. He did not raise his hand, even when he knew the answer.

Why do you think Sam did not raise his hand?
items.answer: Sam was probably shy or nervous because he was new. He did not want to stand out or make a mistake in front of people he did not know yet.

steps: Moving to a new school is hard. Sam sat at the back, which suggests he did not want attention. Not raising his hand, even with the right answer, shows he was worried about how others would see him. New students often feel this way until they feel comfortable.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco's dog Biscuit ran away. Marco looked for him all afternoon. When Biscuit came home on his own, Marco hugged him and started to cry.

Why do you think Marco cried even though Biscuit came back safely?
items.answer: Marco cried because he was so relieved and happy. Sometimes people cry when something scary is over and the person or pet they love is safe.

steps: Marco searched all afternoon, which means he was very worried. When Biscuit came back, the fear and worry that had built up needed somewhere to go. People sometimes cry from relief, not just from sadness. Marco's tears show how much he loved Biscuit and how worried he had been.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Every day, Zoe's teacher gave a star sticker to the student who tried hardest. Zoe never got a star because she was too quiet. One day, Zoe raised her hand and got every answer right. The teacher gave her two stars.

What do the two stars tell you about what the teacher noticed?
items.answer: The two stars show the teacher saw how hard Zoe tried by taking the risk of raising her hand. The teacher wanted to encourage Zoe's effort, not just her correct answers.

steps: The teacher usually gave one star for trying hard. Giving Zoe two stars is unusual and means something special happened. Zoe had been quiet, so raising her hand was a big step. The teacher probably gave two stars because Zoe showed both bravery (raising her hand) and knowledge (right answers). The extra star rewarded her courage.
